walkthroughs.body_html:
Human Geography: Development — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Human Geography: Development brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Human Geography: Development.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is HDI a better measure of development than GNI per capita?
options: Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
HDI combines income, life expectancy and education, capturing quality of life — GNI per capita is just average income and hides inequality and non-economic wellbeing.
Because HDI measures how happy people are.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
